key_insight: DynaFLIP moves motion understanding into the perception module itself, so robots learn representations that are already tuned to action-relevant dynamics rather than only static appearance. It does this by jointly learning from images, language, and 3D flow, making perception more useful for manipulation.
problem_solved: Most robot perception models are pre-trained for object recognition or vision-language alignment, which captures what things look like but not how they move or how actions change the scene. This paper addresses the gap between static visual understanding and the dynamic information needed for robot manipulation.
method: Builds tri-modal training data composed of image-language-3D flow triplets from heterogeneous human and robotic sources.
Uses dynamics-guided multimodal pre-training so the encoder learns motion-aware representations upstream in perception.
Aligns visual, linguistic, and 3D motion cues to preserve action-relevant scene information for downstream robot policies.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in robotics, this suggests a stronger foundation for manipulation tasks by improving the quality of learned perception features. It can reduce reliance on downstream policies to infer motion from scratch and may improve transfer to real-world, dynamic environments.

paper_title: DynaFLIP: Rethinking Robotics Perception via Tri-Modal-Dynamics Guided Representation
paper_authors: Jusuk Lee, Seungjae Lee, Jonghun Shin, Hoseong Jung, Sungha Kim
